review.summary: Fix for a method dispatch ambiguity regression where `defaultalg(::WOperator, ::GPUArray, ::OperatorAssumptions)` threw a MethodError due to two equally-specific method candidates. The fix adds the missing intersection method and cleans up QA-related import issues.
review.evidence: The linked issue #1240 clearly describes a MethodError ambiguity that caused runtime failures on `main`. The error is reproducible: calling `defaultalg` with a `WOperator` and a GPU array (JLArray) throws an ambiguity error. The fix adds the missing intersection method in `src/default.jl` to resolve the dispatch. A regression test (`test/Core/forwarddiff_gpu.jl`) is included that covers the ambiguous dispatch path using `JLArray` (a CPU-backed GPU array stand-in).
review.missing_evidence: The actual diff content is not available, so I cannot inspect the precise code changes in `src/default.jl` and `src/LinearSolve.jl`. The commit also includes QA cleanup (removing stale import, updating ExplicitImports inventories) which are non-bug changes bundled with the fix, but these are minor housekeeping tied to the same regression.
review.validation_risks: The commit bundles QA cleanup (stale import removal, ExplicitImports inventory updates) alongside the actual bug fix, which slightly complicates isolation. The test uses `JLArray` as a GPU array proxy, which may not perfectly replicate real GPU dispatch behavior. The `test/qa/qa.jl` changes may be environment-sensitive depending on which extensions are loaded.
review.suggested_tests: 1. Test that `defaultalg(WOperator{true}(...), JLArray(ones(2)), OperatorAssumptions(true))` returns KrylovJL_GMRES without throwing. 2. Test that the non-GPU path `defaultalg(WOperator{true}(...), ones(2), OperatorAssumptions(true))` still works correctly. 3. Run ExplicitImports/Aqua QA checks to confirm no regressions.
